title: Energy storage capacity increase
engineering_question: A design parameter on the energy storage system has been increased. What is the engineering impact and what must now be re-verified?
one_liner: Assess the impact of this engineering change.
initial_input: Engineering change ECR-001 proposes increasing HV cell capacity from 68 Ah to 75 Ah, raising usable pack energy from 78.0 kWh to 86.0 kWh at unchanged pack envelope, with a chemistry move from NMC622 to NMC811.
expected_impacted_domains: Thermal management capacity at increased energy and heat generation
Charging strategy and charge time at revised cell characteristics
Vehicle mass and axle load distribution
Tyre load index adequacy at revised axle load
BMS estimation models calibrated on the previous chemistry
expected_reasoning_paths: ECR-001 AFFECTS COMP-001 which is part of SUB-001 within SYS-001, so requirements allocated to SYS-001 are candidates for impact
Higher usable energy increases pack mass, which propagates to REQ-002 kerb mass and REQ-003 axle load, and from there to REQ-121 tyre load capability
Chemistry change invalidates the BMS estimation calibration behind REQ-017 and REQ-013, so FM-020 and FM-023 become live again
Existing evidence TR-042 and TR-044 was generated on the 68 Ah cell and is therefore not transferable
known_unknowns: TEST-004 accelerated ageing acceptance criterion is TBD_PROGRAMME_SPECIFIC for the revised chemistry
TEST-025 state-of-health correlation acceptance band is not established
No cell characterisation data for the 75 Ah cell exists in the environment
Revised pack mass value is not stated in ECR-001; only that the envelope is unchanged
Crash load path implications of increased pack mass are not represented in the environment
data_classification: SIMULATED ENTERPRISE ARTEFACT - not OEM, customer or proprietary data
